name: a_movers_premarket
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Topic: After-hours & pre-market movers.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 4:00 PM ET (after the close) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
US stocks >= $1B moving after hours on the session date and pre-market on the brief date: % move, time quoted, and catalyst (earnings, offerings, M&A, guidance, rating changes, withdrawn deals).

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **IBKR** — Financial Services
- Shares fell 1% after hours on Oct. 15 after third-quarter adjusted EPS was $0.67 versus $0.68 consensus; revenue was $1.91 billion versus $1.87 billion expected. (CNBC, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[1]

## **JBHT** — Transportation
- Shares declined more than 2% after hours after third-quarter EPS was $1.82 versus $1.89 consensus; revenue was $3.68 billion versus $3.57 billion expected. (CNBC, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[1]

## **AA** — Metals & Mining
- Shares gained 2% after hours after third-quarter adjusted EPS was $1.82 versus $1.47 consensus; revenue was $3.70 billion versus $3.79 billion expected. (CNBC, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[1]

## **VRNS** — Software & SaaS
- Shares gained more than 2% after hours after Proofpoint announced an all-cash acquisition of Varonis valued at approximately $6.3 billion; closing was expected in the first half of 2027. (CNBC, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[2]

## **KMB** — Retail / Consumer Staples
- Shares gained about 4% during Oct. 15 trading after preliminary third-quarter adjusted EPS of $1.70 versus $1.58 FactSet consensus and revenue of $4.13 billion versus $4.09 billion expected. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]
- Shares gained 1.8% in premarket trading after preliminary third-quarter net sales of $4.13 billion versus $4.10 billion consensus and adjusted EPS of $1.70 versus $1.60 expected. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## **PAG** — Automotive Retail
- Shares gained 8% during Oct. 15 trading after the company announced a definitive agreement to be taken private by Motown Acquisition Corp., owned by Penske Corp. and Mitsui, for $212 per share in cash. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]
- Shares gained 8.6% in premarket trading following the announced $212-per-share cash transaction. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## **RKLB** — Aerospace
- Shares fell 11% during Oct. 15 trading after the company delayed the first launch of its Neutron rocket to 2027. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]
- Shares fell 9.4% in premarket trading to $53.60 after the company disclosed that Neutron’s first launch had been pushed into 2027. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## **FMC** — Chemicals
- Shares fell 32% during Oct. 15 trading after the company cut third-quarter revenue guidance to $65 million–$125 million from a FactSet consensus of $868.5 million. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]

## **WMT** — Retail
- Shares gained more than 2% during Oct. 15 trading after Deutsche Bank upgraded the stock to Buy from Hold, citing a positive 2027 outlook. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]

## **CROX** — Retail / Footwear
- Shares gained 6% during Oct. 15 trading after Barclays upgraded Crocs to Overweight from Equal Weight. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]

## **MRSH** — Insurance
- Shares gained 5% during Oct. 15 trading after third-quarter adjusted EPS was $2.03 versus $1.97 FactSet consensus and revenue was $6.86 billion versus $6.64 billion expected. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET)[7]

## **CRWV** — AI Infrastructure
- Shares fell 2% during Oct. 15 trading as CoreWeave’s debt-funded AI infrastructure expansion remained a market focus; Reuters reported that its credit-default-swap spread exceeded 1,000 basis points on Oct. 15. (CNBC, Oct. 15 12:46 ET; Reuters, Oct. 15, publish time not shown)[7][8]
- Shares fell 6% in premarket trading on Oct. 15 after falling more than 15% on Oct. 14 amid concerns about debt-funded expansion. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## Semiconductors — **NVDA**, **AMD**, **INTC**, **MU**, **WDC**, **STX**
- Micron shares fell 4.1%, Western Digital and Seagate each fell more than 4%, Nvidia fell 1.8%, and Intel and AMD each fell more than 3% in premarket trading on Oct. 15. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## **Venture Global** — Energy
- Shares gained 1.6% in premarket trading on Oct. 15 after the company signed agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes Energy Services to expand power-generation capabilities. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

## **RELX** — Information Services
- Shares gained 2.6% in premarket trading to $37.87 after Bank of America Securities reaffirmed its Buy rating and 4,000-pence price target. (Investing.com, Oct. 15; publish time not shown)[5]

*The available results identify Oct. 15 premarket items and Oct. 15 after-hours items, but do not provide a verified set of quotations published between the Oct. 15 close and the Oct. 16 02:03 ET cutoff.*
